m_Descriptor.title: Player: Graphics Jobs
m_Descriptor.description: The Graphics Jobs option in Player Settings is disabled.
m_Descriptor.solution:
Try enabling it and testing your application. This option spreads the task of building the render command buffer every frame across as many CPU cores as possible, rather than performing all the work in the render thread which is often a bottleneck. Performance will vary depending on the project.

Note: This feature is experimental on specific Unity versions and may introduce new crashes. It is recommended to test accordingly.

m_Descriptor.title: Player: Prebake Collision Meshes
m_Descriptor.description: The Prebake Collision Meshes option in Player Settings is disabled.
m_Descriptor.solution: If you are using physics in your application, consider enabling this option. Prebaked collision meshes can result in an increase in build times and sizes, but reduce loading/initialization times in your application, because serializing prebaked meshes is faster than baking them at runtime.

m_Descriptor.title: Player: Mipmap Stripping
m_Descriptor.description: The Texture MipMap Stripping option in Player Settings is disabled. The generated build might be larger than necessary.
m_Descriptor.solution: Enable Texture MipMap Stripping. Note that this feature will only reduce the build size if no quality levels on the platform use highest mip(s). Furthermore, if code drives the masterTextureLevel to a value higher than those in the quality level settings the mip will no longer be available if this is enabled.

m_Descriptor.title: Physics2D: Layer Collision Matrix
m_Descriptor.description: In Physics 2D Settings, all of the boxes in the Layer Collision Matrix are ticked. This increases the CPU work that Unity must do when calculating collision detections.
m_Descriptor.solution: Un-tick all of the boxes except the ones that represent collisions that should be considered by the 2D physics system.

m_Descriptor.title: Physics2D: Simulation Mode
m_Descriptor.description: UnityEngine.Physics2D.simulationMode is set to either FixedUpdate or Update. By using this mode, 2D physics simulation is executed on every update which might be expensive for some projects.
m_Descriptor.solution: Change Project Settings ➔ Physics 2D ➔ General Settings ➔ Simulation Mode to Script to disable the 2d physics processing each frame. If physics simulation is required for certain special rendering, use Script mode to control Physics2d.Simulate on a per frame basis.

m_Descriptor.title: Physics: Layer Collision Matrix
m_Descriptor.description: In Physics Settings, all of the boxes in the Layer Collision Matrix are ticked. This increases the CPU work that Unity must do when calculating collision detections.
m_Descriptor.solution: Un-tick all of the boxes except the ones that represent collisions that should be considered by the physics system.

m_Descriptor.title: Audio: Speaker Mode
m_Descriptor.description: UnityEngine.AudioSettings.speakerMode is not set to UnityEngine.AudioSpeakerMode.Mono. The generated build will be larger than necessary.
m_Descriptor.solution: To reduce runtime memory consumption of AudioClips change Project Settings ➔ Audio ➔ Default Speaker Mode to Mono. This will half memory usage of stereo AudioClips. It is also recommended considering enabling the Force To Mono AudioClip import setting to reduce import times and build size.

m_Descriptor.title: Quality: Quality Levels
m_Descriptor.description: This project is using the default set of quality levels defined in Project Settings ➔ Quality.
m_Descriptor.solution: Check the quality setting for each platform the project supports in the grid - it's the level with the green tick. Remove quality levels you are not using, to make the Quality Settings simpler to see and edit. Adjust the setting for each platform if necessary, then select the appropriate levels to examine their settings in the panel below.

m_Descriptor.title: Quality: Texture Quality
m_Descriptor.description: One or more of the quality levels in the project's Quality Settings has Texture Quality set to something other than Full Res. This option can save memory on lower-spec devices and platforms by discarding higher-resolution mip levels on mipmapped textures before uploading them to the GPU. However, this option has no effect on textures which don't have mipmaps enabled (as is frequently the case with UI textures, for instance), does nothing to reduce download or install size, and gives you no control over the texture resize algorithm.
m_Descriptor.solution: For devices which must use lower-resolution versions of textures, consider creating these lower resolution textures separately, and choosing the appropriate content to load at runtime using AssetBundle variants.

m_Descriptor.title: Quality: Async Upload Time Slice
m_Descriptor.description: The Async Upload Time Slice option for one or more quality levels in the project's Quality Settings is set to the default value of 2ms.
m_Descriptor.solution: If the project encounters long loading times when loading large amount of texture and/or mesh data, experiment with increasing this value to see if it allows content to be uploaded to the GPU more quickly.

m_Descriptor.title: Quality: Async Upload Buffer Size
m_Descriptor.description: The Async Upload Buffer Size option for one or more quality levels in the project's Quality Settings is set to the default value.
m_Descriptor.solution: If the project encounters long loading times when loading large amount of texture and/or mesh data, experiment with increasing this value to see if it allows content to be uploaded to the GPU more quickly. This is most likely to help if you are loading large textures. Note that this setting controls a buffer size in megabytes, so exercise caution if memory is limited in your application.

m_Descriptor.title: Time: Fixed Timestep
m_Descriptor.description: In the Time Settings, Fixed Timestep is set to the default value of 0.02. This means that Unity will try to ensure that the FixedUpdate() methods of MonoBehaviours, and physics updates will be called 50 times per second. This is appropriate for games running at 60 FPS, but at 30 FPS this would mean that the FixedUpdate step will be called twice during most frames.
m_Descriptor.solution: We recommend setting Fixed Timestep to 0.04 when running at 30 FPS, in order to call the fixed updates at 25 Hz. The reason for having the fixed update be slightly less than the target frame rate is to avoid the “spiral of death”, in which if one frame takes longer than 33.3ms, FixedUpdate() happens multiple times on the next frame to catch up, pushing that frame time over as well, and permanently locking the game into a state where it cannot reach the desired frame rate because FixedUpdate() is constantly trying to catch up.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: UnityEngine.GameObject.GetComponentsInChildren
m_Descriptor.description: Some versions of GameObject.GetComponentsInChildren() allocate managed memory.
m_Descriptor.solution: Ensure you are using one of the versions of GameObject.GetComponentsInChildren() which accepts a List as a parameter and populates it with the components it finds.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'double' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.Log / Debug.LogFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.Log methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: UnityEngine.ImageConversion.LoadImage
m_Descriptor.description: ImageConversion.LoadImage() defaults to maintaining a CPU-accessible copy of the image. This is a waste of memory if not needed.
m_Descriptor.solution: If a CPU-accessible copy of the texture is not required, ensure that the markNonReadable flag passed into the method is set to true.

m_Descriptor.title: UnityEngine.Texture2D.GetPixels32
m_Descriptor.description: Texture2D.GetPixels32() allocates managed memory.
m_Descriptor.solution: Use Texture2D.GetRawTextureData() instead. This method returns a NativeArray of pixel data, and so does not allocate managed memory.

m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: UnityEngine.Renderer.material
m_Descriptor.description: The Renderer.material property creates a unique copy of the Renderer's material. This breaks draw call batching and results in a higher number of draw calls, impacting rendering performance.
m_Descriptor.solution: If possible, use Renderer.sharedMaterial instead.

m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.solution: We strongly advise against using Linq in any frequently-updated code. Ban its usage from the project entirely, or confine it to initialization code and use it sparingly.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.Log / Debug.LogFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.Log methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.Log / Debug.LogFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.Log methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'float' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'Int32' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: System.Reflection.*
m_Descriptor.description: Reflection is slow, and not generally considered performant enough for runtime code.
m_Descriptor.solution: Remove code which relies on reflection, or minimise its usage, particularly outside of initialization.

m_Descriptor.description: Debug.Log methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'T' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'MemberTypes' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid allocating objects in frequently-updated code.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'Boolean' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'TProperty' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'TField' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type

m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: Debug.LogWarning / Debug.LogWarningFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'T' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Warning, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Debug.LogWarning methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. m_Descriptor.title: Debug.Log / Debug.LogFormat
m_Descriptor.description: Debug.Log methods cause slowdowns, especially if used frequently.
m_Descriptor.solution: Instead of removing code an option is to strip this code on release builds by using scripting symbols for conditional compilation (#if ... #endif) or the ConditionalAttribute on a method where you call this. When logging is still used in your code a small optimization can be to leave out the callstack, if not required, by setting Application.SetStackTraceLogType(LogType.Log, StackTraceLogType.None) via code.

m_Issues.m_Description: Conversion from value type 'T' to ref type

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.title: Boxing Allocation
m_Descriptor.messageFormat: Conversion from value type '{0}' to ref type
m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.

m_Descriptor.description: Boxing happens where a value type, such as an integer, is converted into an object of reference type. This causes an allocation on the heap, which might increase the size of the managed heap and the frequency of Garbage Collection.
m_Descriptor.solution: Try to avoid Boxing when possible.
